classification.difficultyReason: Requires denominator restrictions, positive-square multiplication and graphical analysis, including an isolated equality solution.

inlines.text: and sketch the resulting cubic; exclude

answer.worked:
The restriction is $x\ne0$, so $x^2>0$. Multiplying by $x^2$ gives
$$\begin{align*}
2x&\ge(2x+3)x^2\\
x(2x^2+3x-2)&\le0\\
x(2x-1)(x+2)&\le0.
\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=x(2x-1)(x+2)$, with zeroes $-2$, $0$ and $\tfrac12$. The graph is on or below the $x$-axis when $x\le-2$ or $0\le x\le\tfrac12$. Excluding $x=0$ gives
$$x\le-2\quad\text{or}\quad0<x\le\frac12.$$

answer.worked:
The restriction is $x\ne3$, so $(x-3)^2>0$. Multiplying by $(x-3)^2$ gives
$$\begin{align*}
(x+9)(x-3)&\le(x+2)(x-3)^2\\
(x-3)\big[(x+2)(x-3)-(x+9)\big]&\ge0\\
(x-3)(x^2-2x-15)&\ge0\\
(x-3)(x+3)(x-5)&\ge0.
\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=(x-3)(x+3)(x-5)$, with zeroes $-3$, $3$ and $5$. The graph is on or above the $x$-axis when $-3\le x\le3$ or $x\ge5$. Excluding $x=3$ gives
$$-3\le x<3\quad\text{or}\quad x\ge5.$$

spec.mathematics: y=(x-3)(x+3)(x-5); roots -3, 3, 5. The plotted ordinate is 0.06 times the polynomial, preserving roots and signs. Original domain excludes x=3.

answer.worked:
The restriction is $x\ne-1$, so $(x+1)^2>0$. Multiplying by $(x+1)^2$ gives
$$\begin{align*}
(x-2)(x+1)&\ge(x-1)(x+1)^2\\
(x+1)\big[(x-1)(x+1)-(x-2)\big]&\le0\\
(x+1)(x^2-x+1)&\le0.
\end{align*}$$
Since
$$x^2-x+1=\left(x-\frac12\right)^2+\frac34,$$
the quadratic factor is always positive. Sketch $y=(x+1)(x^2-x+1)=x^3+1$, whose only zero is $-1$. The graph is on or below the $x$-axis for $x\le-1$. Excluding $x=-1$ gives
$$x<-1.$$

spec.description: Authored solution sketch of y=x^3+1. The negative portion is blue and its boundary is open because the original denominator vanishes.
spec.mathematics: y=(x+1)(x^2-x+1)=x^3+1; unique real zero -1. The quadratic factor is strictly positive. Original domain excludes x=-1.

answer.worked:
The restriction is $x\ne1$, so $(1-x)^2>0$. Multiplying by $(1-x)^2$ gives
$$\begin{align*}
1-x&\le(x+1)(1-x)^2\\
(1-x)\big[(x+1)(1-x)-1\big]&\ge0\\
-x^2(1-x)&\ge0\\
x^2(x-1)&\ge0.
\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=x^2(x-1)$. It touches the $x$-axis at $x=0$ and crosses at $x=1$. The graph is on or above the $x$-axis when $x=0$ or $x\ge1$. Excluding $x=1$ gives
$$x=0\quad\text{or}\quad x>1.$$
